def: A template argument of `extents` (or the `Extent` of `span`) that is not equal to `dynamic_extent`: the length of that dimension is fixed at compile time and occupies no storage in the object.
An extent template argument whose value is `dynamic_extent` (i.e. `numeric_limits<size_t>::max()`): the length of that dimension is supplied at run time and stored in the object.

The Cartesian product of a number of half-open integer intervals `[Lᵢ, Uᵢ)`. The number of intervals is the rank; the size is the product of the interval lengths, and is 1 when the rank is 0. `extents` represents such a space (with lower bounds always 0).

A callable object mapping a multidimensional index to a one-dimensional offset; it must provide `extents()`, `required_span_size()`, and queries for properties such as unique/exhaustive/strided. The `LayoutPolicy::mapping<E>` of `mdspan` is such a type.

A type specifying how to obtain an element reference from a data handle `p` and offset `i` (`access(p, i)`) and how to advance the handle (`offset(p, i)`); the data handle need not be a pointer, nor the reference `T&`.

For a given data handle and accessor, `[0, N)` is its accessible range if the access function yields a valid reference for every `i ∈ [0, N)`. A precondition of the `mdspan` constructors requires `[0, required_span_size())` to be an accessible range.

A range whose iterators' validity does not depend on the lifetime of the range object itself (e.g. `span`, `string_view`, lvalue references). Ranges algorithms return real iterators rather than `ranges::dangling` for rvalue borrowed ranges.
